programme: Twelve-week API Foundations, Platform & Reliability Engineering

assumptions.api_experience: Assume no current API-building experience and no reliable recall of FastAPI; teach HTTP and API design first, then build the app step by step.
assumptions.python_experience: Do not schedule Python fundamentals. Assume the learner knows Python and can read/write ordinary application code; only cover environment and dependency setup as needed for the project.
assumptions.optional_extensions: Selected sessions include an optional 15-minute stretch; never required.
assumptions.project_approach: Start with the request/response model and endpoint contract before implementing routes. Avoid large code dumps; build one endpoint at a time and explain each decision.

cadence.first_week_exception: Start Tuesday 24 November 2026; Week 1 has five study sessions (Tuesday–Saturday). Sundays remain review/rest days.

days.title: API lab setup and first FastAPI process
days.objective: Verify the existing Colima/Docker setup without changing it; check Python/Git versions; create the reliability-lab-api folder and virtual environment; install FastAPI; create a minimal app and run it locally.
days.deliverable: A minimal FastAPI application running locally, a clean project folder, .venv excluded from Git, and /docs opening in the browser.
days.notes: Completed and verified interactively. Colima started successfully; Docker uses the colima context and the Docker CLI discovers the Homebrew Compose plugin. Python 3.14.2 and Git 2.56.1 available. Created reliability-lab-api with an active .venv, .gitignore excluding .venv and Python cache files, and installed FastAPI 0.165.0 (fastapi[standard]). Created main.py with GET / returning {"message":"Hello, world!"}. FastAPI dev server started at http://127.0.0.1:8000; terminal logs confirm GET /, /docs, and /openapi.json returned HTTP 200. favicon.ico 404 is harmless.

inspect JSON responses and content types.

days.deliverable: A method-to-action table for the Task API and curl examples for GET and POST against a public test API.

days.title: API contract and manual test pass
days.objective: Define response models; check /docs and /openapi.json; exercise every endpoint using curl or Swagger UI; record example requests.

days.objective: Refresh tables, rows, columns, primary keys, uniqueness and basic SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE; inspect SQLite with Python.

days.objective: Follow FastAPI SQL database tutorial; install SQLModel; define Task table model; create SQLite engine and database file.
days.deliverable: A Task table is created from the model in the lab.

days.title: Database sessions and dependencies

days.title: Persist task creation and listing

days.deliverable: POST and GET /tasks use SQLite persistence.

days.title: Persist retrieve, update and delete
days.objective: Convert task detail, PATCH and DELETE endpoints to database operations; handle nonexistent IDs and commit changes.
days.deliverable: All CRUD operations work against SQLite across app restarts.

days.title: Database integrity and persistence checks
days.objective: Test unique IDs and required fields; inspect SQLite file; test fresh DB creation and invalid input; document limitations.
days.deliverable: Repeatable persistence check and database notes; no migration framework required yet.
days.extension_task: Add one test for a task that remains available after recreating the app process.

days.title: Refactor into a small app structure
days.objective: Separate main app, task routes, schemas, database and models; use APIRouter; keep layout small and readable.
days.deliverable: A modular FastAPI app with the same behaviour as before refactor.

days.title: Pydantic schemas and response models
days.objective: Separate create, update and response schemas; prevent internal DB fields leaking accidentally; validate input lengths and required values.
days.deliverable: Explicit input/output schemas and predictable response JSON.

days.title: pytest fundamentals

days.title: FastAPI TestClient and endpoint tests

days.deliverable: A repeatable API test suite that runs with one command.

days.title: Error handling, dependencies and configuration

days.deliverable: Consistent 404/422 behaviours and documented local configuration example.

days.title: Logging, health checks and API checkpoint

days.title: OpenTelemetry and Jaeger independent trace investigation
days.objective: Run the API with OpenTelemetry instrumentation, generate requests and use Jaeger to inspect trace IDs, spans, parent/child relationships and duration. Relate trace IDs to application log context where configured.
days.deliverable: Two annotated trace examples: one normal request and one slower/failing request, with a short explanation of spans and trace context.
tasks: Start only Jaeger and the instrumented API
Generate a normal request and inspect its trace
Generate a second request with a controlled delay or error
Compare spans, duration and trace context
Check whether trace_id/span_id can be found in corresponding logs

days.title: Grafana dashboard, alert and SLO quality review
days.objective: Review whether the dashboard and alerts help an on-call engineer decide what to do. Improve labels/units/thresholds, check pending/firing/recovery/no-data behaviour, and explain the learning SLO and its error budget.
days.deliverable: Reviewed dashboard JSON, tested alert/runbook and an SLO note with explicit lab limitations.
tasks: Review request, error, latency and availability panels
Check legends, units, labels and dashboard readability
Trigger and recover one alert; inspect no-data behaviour
Review the SLI/SLO calculation and measurement window
Write one concrete on-call action for each alert

days.title: Independent end-to-end incident response drill
days.objective: Choose one controlled local-only failure scenario and investigate it without a step-by-step guide. Use available metric, log, trace and Kubernetes evidence; recover the service and verify the result.
days.deliverable: A fourth incident exercise or tabletop report showing detection, timeline, evidence, diagnosis, mitigation, recovery and prevention.
tasks: Select one local-only fault: unavailable target, HTTP 5xx, latency, bad rollout or failing probe
Detect the issue and identify its user/service impact
Collect relevant metrics, logs, traces and Kubernetes evidence where applicable
Mitigate, restore and verify service health
Write the incident timeline and follow-up actions

days.title: Final independent capstone and portfolio review
days.objective: Starting from a clean state, demonstrate the Task API, container build/Compose networking, Kubernetes operation and the three observability signals. Explain design choices and limits as if presenting to an SRE/platform engineering interviewer.
days.deliverable: Reproducible project README, clean manifests/configuration, dashboard and alert exports, incident reports and a five-minute capstone walkthrough.
tasks: Start from documented clean-state instructions
Demonstrate API CRUD, validation, tests and persistence
Demonstrate Docker build, Compose, volume and network behaviour
Demonstrate Kubernetes deployment, troubleshooting, rollout and rollback
Demonstrate Prometheus metrics, Loki logs, OpenTelemetry traces and Grafana
Present three required incident reports plus the additional drill/tabletop
Write an honest self-assessment of independent skills and production gaps

weekly_reviews.title: Week 1 review — HTTP foundations and first API setup
weekly_reviews.expected_outcome: Set up the project and explain request/response anatomy, URLs, methods and status codes.
checks: Link or identify the deliverable that works; do not count reading alone.
Can I explain request/response lifecycle, URL structure, methods and status code groups?
What did I get running locally and what evidence proves it?
Which concept still feels unfamiliar? Write one precise question.
Did I stay close to the 60-minute target?
Explain one concept aloud in 2–3 minutes without notes.

weekly_reviews.title: Week 2 review — REST contract and FastAPI fundamentals
weekly_reviews.expected_outcome: Complete the API contract and create routes using path/query parameters and Pydantic models.
checks: Link api-contract.md and the working FastAPI routes/docs.
Can I explain each resource, route, path/query parameter and request model?
Can I use /docs and inspect /openapi.json?
What did I build without copying the complete example?
Which validation behaviour remains unclear?
Did I preserve the Sunday rest/review?

weekly_reviews.title: Week 3 review — Build the Task API: CRUD
weekly_reviews.expected_outcome: Implement create/list/retrieve/update/delete and consistent validation/error behaviour.
checks: Link the working CRUD endpoints and manual test evidence.
Can I create, list, retrieve, update and delete tasks without a tutorial?
Are missing IDs and invalid input handled predictably?
What does each endpoint return and with which status code?
What failed and how did I prove the fix?
What should be repeated before persistence?

weekly_reviews.title: Week 4 review — Persist API data with SQLite
weekly_reviews.expected_outcome: Use SQLModel, sessions and dependencies so data survives restarts.
checks: Link models, database/session code and persistence evidence.
Can I explain engine, model, session, dependency and commit?
Does data survive an application restart?
Did I test integrity/duplicate or invalid records?
What database concept needs another pass?
What can I now perform independently?

weekly_reviews.title: Week 5 review — Test and harden the API
weekly_reviews.expected_outcome: Refactor, write tests, configure errors/logging/health and verify the service.
checks: Link tests, config, logging and health endpoint evidence.
Can I run tests and interpret failures?
Do tests use an isolated test database?
Are errors and health/readiness behaviour clear?
What did I refactor and why?
Is the API ready to containerise?

weekly_reviews.title: Week 6 review — API checkpoint and Docker foundations
weekly_reviews.expected_outcome: Checkpoint the API and build/run the first container, inspect it and persist data.
checks: Link Dockerfile, image, Compose file and volume test.
Can I build/run/inspect the image?
Can I explain writable layer vs named volume?
Does the API work through a published port?
Did I verify Colima and Compose work without Docker Desktop?
What will I practise next week?

weekly_reviews.title: Week 7 review — Docker networking and Kubernetes fundamentals
weekly_reviews.expected_outcome: Complete Compose networking and deploy Kubernetes workloads, Services and rollouts.
checks: Link Compose network and Kubernetes manifests.
Can containers communicate by service name?
Can I explain Pod, Deployment, ReplicaSet and Service?
Can I verify selectors/endpoints and perform a rollout/rollback?
Why does the SQLite API stay at one replica?
What differed between browser and local labs?

weekly_reviews.title: Week 8 review — Kubernetes operations and troubleshooting
weekly_reviews.expected_outcome: Operate probes, resources, storage, RBAC and diagnose failure states.
checks: Link the Kubernetes runbook and failure matrix.
Can I distinguish liveness, readiness and startup probes?
Can I explain requests, limits and OOMKilled evidence?
Can I prove one allowed and one denied RBAC action?
Which failures did I diagnose and what evidence proved each cause?
What needs repeating independently?

weekly_reviews.title: Week 9 review — Kubernetes checkpoint and observability foundations
weekly_reviews.expected_outcome: Run the cluster runbook and learn metrics, logs and traces.
checks: Link /metrics, promql.md, LogQL queries, trace evidence and cluster runbook.
Can I explain what metrics, logs and traces each tell me?
Can I query request rate, 5xx ratio and latency in PromQL?
Can I find application errors in Loki with LogQL?
Can I inspect a request trace and explain its spans?
What is still guided rather than independent?

weekly_reviews.title: Week 10 review — Metrics, logs, traces, alerting and incident response
weekly_reviews.expected_outcome: Query metrics/logs/traces, build rules/dashboard/alerts, and complete the three required incident drills: target unavailable, elevated HTTP 5xx and elevated latency.
checks: Link dashboard JSON, alert runbook, SLO note and incident report 1.
Can I use Grafana to assess request rate, errors, latency and availability?
Can I move from an alert/time window to related logs and traces?
Incident 1: target unavailable — report complete?
Incident 2: elevated HTTP 5xx — report complete?
Incident 3: elevated latency — report complete?
Are faults local-only and has normal service state been restored?

weekly_reviews.title: Week 11 review — Independent container and Kubernetes labs
weekly_reviews.expected_outcome: Repeat Docker and Kubernetes work from a clean state; break/fix and document evidence.
checks: Link clean-state Docker/Kubernetes runbooks and failure records.
Can I rebuild and redeploy from documentation alone?
Can I diagnose container network/volume problems independently?
Can I deploy a workload and diagnose a planted Kubernetes failure?
Can I roll back and prove RBAC permissions?
What still requires step-by-step guidance?
Which exercise should receive one more repetition?

weekly_reviews.title: Week 12 review — Independent observability and final capstone
weekly_reviews.expected_outcome: Investigate metrics/logs/traces, improve alert quality, run an independent incident and present the project.
checks: Link updated README, dashboards, alert, all incident reports and capstone notes.
Can I investigate metrics, logs and traces without a step-by-step guide?
Can I explain alert/SLO choices and their limitations?
Is the final demo reproducible from a clean state?
Can I explain platform/SRE trade-offs clearly?
What can I do independently and what still needs production experience?
Choose the next learning priority based on evidence.

migration_note: Revised on 2026-11-23 after learner clarified that Python fundamentals are not needed. Week 1 now covers HTTP/API foundations; Week 2 starts FastAPI directly. No previously completed sessions existed; all 60 sessions remain not_started. Further updated the Week 6–10 lab overlay on 2026-11-23 to add free browser labs paired with local Colima/k3d work, Docker networking, Loki/Alloy logs, OpenTelemetry/Jaeger traces and three explicit incident drills. Existing progress statuses and notes were preserved. Rebased on 2026-11-23 for a Tuesday 2026-11-24 start. Sundays remain review/rest days. Week 1 is a five-session kickoff; Weeks 2–12 each contain six sessions. Added 11 consolidation sessions D61–D71. Existing session statuses were preserved as not_started; finish moved to 2027-02-13 and final review to 2027-02-14.
lab_method: For D31-D71, use a short free browser lab when available (about 10–15 minutes inside the guided-practice block), then reproduce the concept locally and save evidence in this repository. Keep each study session to 60 minutes. Browser environments are disposable; the local project is the source of truth.
browser_lab_safety: Do not enter production credentials, tokens or personal data into public labs. Killercoda free scenarios are time-limited and ephemeral. Public demo datasets can reset.
observability_signals: logs: structured stdout, Grafana Alloy and Loki
